title: Localizing the ordinary isomorphism-square mate, including strict diagrams
statement: For d and a chosen scheme square as in lem-pur-reindexing-ordinary-mate-sections, assume the ordinary purReindexingModuleMate is invertible. Then the specified ambient derived mate and specified strict-diagram derived mate are invertible. On every K-injective completed-module complex I, respectively every K-injective strict tower complex I, each derived mate satisfies the equation obtained by inserting its source right-derived unit, the ordinary mate applied degreewise and localized, and its target right-derived unit, with the canonical exact-pullback localization factors on both sides. The two equations are the literal final two clauses of PurCompletedReindexingSquare; no section formula or construction of a Cartesian witness is asserted. The coefficient datum and the concrete canonical maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and [def-pur-completed-reindexing-data].

proof.text: The inverse module reindexing is exact, so its right adjoint reindexing preserves K-injective complexes. The ordinary mate on such a complex computes the two derived direct images. Localize its transpose. The canonical pullback-composition representative formula and the pre-derived-adjunction fraction formula show that this is the transpose defining the specified ambient exchange. The unit-normalized representative equation follows; localizing the inverse ordinary mate proves invertibility.

Whisker the ordinary mate over the strict index category. Naturality ensures that it commutes with every transition, giving a single invertible transformation of actual strict diagrams. On the small diagram site its transpose is the same square map followed by the diagram counit. Exact reverse reindexing preserves diagram K-injectives. Apply the same fraction formula there to identify the localized transformation with exchangeTowerMate, including its representative unit equation and inverse.
